name: The Unanswered Light

stars.name: Lumen Vagus
stars.notes: Bright F-type main sequence star. Unremarkable in every respect except the orbital arrangement of its fifth planet.

planets.name: Scoria
planets.notes: Tidally locked at 0.15 AU. Dayside surface is partially vitrified from stellar radiation.

planets.name: Candela
planets.notes: Orbits at 0.9 AU. Dense CO2 atmosphere with runaway greenhouse effect. Surface temperature exceeds 600K.

planets.name: Lacuna
planets.notes: Orbits at 1.8 AU within the habitable zone. Breathable atmosphere and liquid water exist, but no life of any kind has been detected—not even prebiotic chemistry.

planets.name: Breviary
planets.notes: Jupiter-analog at 6.3 AU. Cloud bands display unusual regularity. Three moons have subsurface oceans, all sterile.

planets.name: The Vagrant
planets.notes: Orbits at 3.1 AU in a path perpendicular to the ecliptic plane—a 90-degree inclination orbit that should not be stable. It crosses the orbital paths of planets 3 and 4 without gravitational disruption.

anomalies.name: The Vagrant's Orbit
anomalies.notes: The Vagrant crosses the orbital paths of Lacuna and Breviary every 1.7 standard years without gravitational interaction. It behaves as if the other planets do not exist, or as if it exists in a slightly different gravitational frame.

anomalies.name: The Sterile Zone
anomalies.notes: Lacuna has every precondition for life—liquid water, breathable atmosphere, stable temperature—yet is completely sterile. Not merely lifeless, but actively so: introduced biological samples degrade within hours through an unknown mechanism.

anomalies.name: The Beckon Signal
anomalies.notes: A 47-second repeating radio pulse has been detected from The Vagrant since its discovery. The signal encodes no recognizable data structure but is clearly artificial. No power source or transmitter has been located on the planet's surface.

asteroid_belts.name: The Pale Ring
asteroid_belts.notes: Unremarkable Kuiper-analog belt. Composition is consistent with normal system formation.

faction_control.notes: Three survey missions have visited; none have established permanent presence. The biological sterilization effect on Lacuna has discouraged colonization attempts.

history: Surveyed in 2506 by the exploration vessel Perihelion. Lacuna was initially flagged as a high-priority colonization candidate before the sterility effect was discovered.

The 2511 Lacuna Expedition landed a biological test payload on the surface. All organic material—from bacteria to plant seeds—degraded within four to nine hours. The mechanism remains unknown. The expedition recommended quarantine classification.

In 2523, a radio astronomy survey detected The Vagrant's repeating signal. Attempts to triangulate a source point on the planet's surface have failed; the signal appears to originate from the planet's geometric center.
description: The Unanswered Light is a young F-type system that appears almost hospitable until closer examination reveals its wrongness. Lumen Vagus burns brightly at the system's center, illuminating five worlds that range from scorched rock to frozen ice. The third planet, Lacuna, sits perfectly within the habitable zone with breathable air and liquid oceans—a paradise by every metric, except that it destroys any biological material placed upon it. The fifth planet orbits perpendicular to everything else, crossing other planets' paths without consequence.

The system's three anomalies may be connected, though no researcher has established a link. Lacuna's sterility suggests an active process rather than simple absence of life—something on or within the planet breaks down organic chemistry with mechanical precision. The Vagrant's impossible orbit implies it is not fully subject to the system's gravitational rules. And the repeating signal from The Vagrant's core has transmitted without pause for at least seventeen years, calling out to no one in a language no one can read.

The Unanswered Light poses questions that cut to the foundations of astrobiology and physics. Why would a planet with every prerequisite for life actively prevent it? What maintains The Vagrant in its impossible orbit? Who—or what—built a transmitter inside a frozen world, and what is it saying? A properly equipped expedition to Lacuna could determine whether the sterilization is chemical, radiological, or something entirely new. A drilling mission to The Vagrant's core could locate the signal source. Both missions carry obvious risks, and neither has been funded. The system waits, its signal repeating every forty-seven seconds, unanswered.
